searchText: I definitely wouldn't call them "non validating" nodes. They are 100% validating nodes. They are just stateless nodes. A stateless node. As far as clients go, either you run a validator client or you don't. Your execution client is either stateless or it isn't. Do you think we need different name for each of the following? * someone who runs a stateless execution client plus a validator *someone who runs a stateful execution client and a validator * someone who runs a stateless execution client and no validator * someone who runs a stateful execution client and no validator It is a bit of a combinatorial explosion when you try to name all combinations. I would just say, "are you stateless or not" and keep that separate from "are you running a validator client"? I like "staking statefull" and "nonstaking stateless". That way we have two terms with negators, and they can combine in any combination. No need to mention "validator" in there, as I think that just adds confusion since users think of "staking" when they often mean (under current terminology) "running a validator client".
